newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mixed, March lower despite exports.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mixed, March lower despite exports.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled mixed, with nearby March closing down and well below early highs despite a bullish export sales report, traders said.
Wheat gained early after USDA said net wheat export sales during the week ended Jan 16 totaled 590,900 tonnes, above expectations of 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes.

But traders said that unlike previous sessions, when March was buoyed by commercial and commission-related buying, there was no "strong buyer" in the March -- possibly because talk of a large Indian wheat purchase had ebbed by the week's end.
Pre-weekend profit taking was also blamed for the weakness in March.

"We remained firm in here today as export sales figures were friendly. CBOT and KCBT March traded in conjunction today, and this was the first time our March had a lower close in four sessions," a trader said.
KCBT wheat closed one cent lower to 1-1/4 cents higher, with March down 3/4 cent at $4.17. Earlier, March had climbed as high as $4.20-1/2 for a gain of 2-1/2 cents.
Commodity brokers E D & F Man International were among the featured players, bear-spreading 1.5 million May/March at 42 cents per bushel. Man also sold one million March.
